text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert — 15:23 UTC — streaming-sse-prod p99 latency > 2.5s over last 5m, chunk delivery spikes and increased connection churn. Paging oncall: @maya

alex: paging @maya (prod oncall) — getting customer DMs about slow realtime events, triage? :pager:

maya: I'm on. ACK. switching to phone and will start triage in channel. any recent deploys?

raj: not aware of infra deploys in last hour. I see a config push to edge-proxy 2 hours ago but nothing in last 30m. digging logs now.

zoe: monitoring shows p95 ~900ms but p99 jumped to ~3.1s at 15:18 and stayed elevated. error rate for streaming endpoints up ~2.2x.

maya: ok. raj — can you paste the proxy->runtime error samples? 

raj: logs (redacted) show repeated write timeouts and slow write drains to clients, followed by connection resets: 

```
E 2024-06-15T15:18:22Z proxy/stream.go:412 write timeout: write tcp 10.0.3.45:443->10.1.2.78:54832: write: connection reset by peer
W 2024-06-15T15:18:23Z proxy/stream.go:320 slow chunk flush (avg 450ms) for conn_id=xyz
```

raj: also seeing 502/504 spikes between proxy and runtime (~30s windows). client ACKs backlog rising — looks like backpressure from a subset of clients holding connections open and stalling chunk drains.

maya: reproduce locally? any canary failing?

alex: no canary alerts in CI, only prod. telemetry shows a cluster of connections from a single customer IP range with abnormal slow-read behavior.

pm-luis: flagged customer "BrightChat" has reported delayed live updates in last 10m. CS Amy is already contacting them.

amy-cs: confirmed — customer saw streaming updates pause for 10-30s intermittently. They are on EU region, traffic routed through edge-proxy-3.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: (1) increase proxy upstream write timeout to 60s (temporarily), (2) scale proxy pool + turn on streaming-throttle to drop severely slow clients, (3) enable chunk-size fallback mode (smaller chunks) for high-latency clients. executing now.

raj: increasing proxy write timeout on edge-proxy-3 -> set PROXY_UPSTREAM_WRITE_TIMEOUT=60s (was 20s)

```
$ kubectl set env deploy/edge-proxy-3 PROXY_UPSTREAM_WRITE_TIMEOUT=60s -n prod
deployment.apps/edge-proxy-3 updated
```

zoe: scaling proxies by +3 replicas on prod-eu-1

```
$ kubectl scale deploy/edge-proxy-3 --replicas=6 -n prod
```

maya: enabling streaming-throttle policy for heavy connections (threshold 120s idle -> drop)

sre-bot: Streaming throttle rule applied to label region=eu-prod by @maya at 15:27 UTC

raj: also pushed a runtime config to enable smaller chunk writes for connections reporting >500ms read latency: set STREAM_CHUNK_FALLBACK=64KB for affected routes.

```
PATCH /config/runtime
{ "route": "/v1/stream/*", "stream_chunk_size": 65536 }
```

alex: after mitigations p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.4s over 5m, error rate trending down. client backlog decreased per metric 'conn_pending_writes'.

zoe: confirming metrics: p95 ~780ms, p99 ~1.4s at 15:34. connection churn reduced by ~60%.

pm-luis: advising CS to tell BrightChat we have applied temporary mitigations and are continuing investigation; they'll follow up if they still see issues.

amy-cs: pinged customer and they report updates are faster now. asked them to reach out if they see stalls again.

maya: root cause hypothesis: a subset of downstream clients with poor TCP read behaviour (slow readers) caused proxy write buffers to pile up, combined with aggressive proxy write buffering config; this amplified head-of-line stalls and triggered proxy->runtime timeouts.

raj: supporting data: connection read window skew on those client IPs, elevated socket buffers in `ss -tanp` dumps, and slow socket churn correlates with spike windows. Also noticed increased resend/keepalive retries from ALB (proxy front).

zoe: long-term mitigation ideas: (A) improve streaming backpressure handling in runtime to avoid large in-memory buffers, (B) enforce per-conn soft limits + early drop for extremely slow readers, (C) tune ALB/proxy keepalive and write-buffer thresholds, (D) add client-side guidance for chunk pacing.

maya: immediate post-handoff actions: create incident ticket (INC-2024-274), collect packet captures from edge-proxy-3 between 15:12-15:36 UTC, and run targeted canary that simulates slow-reader clients to validate throttle.

alex: I'm creating the ticket and adding links to dashboards + logs.

```
INC-2024-274: https://redwood.prod/incidents/INC-2024-274
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/prod/streaming?from=1719004000&to=1719004700
Logs: https://logs.redwood/prod/_search?q=proxy+write+timeout
```

pm-luis: I'll draft a customer-facing note with Amy, aiming for a 30-min update and a follow-up once we have RCA.

maya: handing to eng-runtime (raj + zoe) for deeper analysis and remediation. I'll stay on watch for 1 hour then hand to follow-up oncall. Closing active paging but keeping incident open.

sre-bot: @oncall_handback — active page cleared by @maya at 15:41 UTC. Follow-up channel: #incidents-INC-2024-274

maya: final status: mitigations applied, p99 improved, primary customer impact reduced. tracking next steps in incident ticket: packet captures, config diff for proxy change, and a postmortem with action items to prevent recurrence.

alex: thanks team. if anyone sees renewed spike, re-page immediately. :thumbsup:

maya: handing off to follow-up oncall (zoe) for postmortem coordination.

zoe: taking follow-up. will collect artifacts and schedule RCA meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC. adding CS note and owners for code changes.

incident-bot: Incident state updated -> monitoring (owner: zoe).
